answers.text: The following interviews were created by a.i. when prompted to portay people with interesting jobs answering the question, “What is your biggest problem”
As always, a representative sample of answers is shown:-repeats-glitches -nonsense answers so that unfamiliar viewers can become more familiar with the technology
-What is your problem in life? Time Apples don't care about my schedule. They ripen when they please, rot when they please If I miss their moment, all I get is vinegar and regret.
Honestly, people Not in a bad way, just folks see the bird and they want to touch her or get a selfie two inches from her face They forget she’s not a pet she’s a razor with feathers
Fall in love with things that burn out Lamps, fireworks, people who go too hard, too fast I make neon for a living... Most of it dies in a couple of years
I keep wanting everything to stay in perfect order. But bees teach you, nothing stays put. I spend most of my days convincing creatures with stingers not to hate me

And then I come home and can't convince myself of the same thing I keep trying to hold heat the way I hold a tool I want it precise, obedient, but it slides through every gap I leave I keep trying to hold on to things that were born to be molten
Kids grow up. Friends drift. Glass cools. Volcanic plumes build static like a giant battery. When it discharges,
the lightning can fry aircraft avionics or set off gas pipelines miles away This volcano wakes fast. If the flank gives way, that river of lava could cut right through the town in the valley. Dust
one storm and the sensors read a sunrise at midnight Creeps under seals. Clings to charge and the data goes wild -What is your problem? Salt eats metal faster than the tide turns.

One storm can pit a gear, seize a bearing, and the whole clock drifts out of truth Tides are creeping higher. And the heat steals the water too fast. These ponds used to give us a season Now they give us a month
-What's your biggest problem out here? The ocean won't stay still It keeps trying to pull everything apart. Lines, anchors, whole rows of crop I can hear storms coming before everyone else does.

That's good for the job, but lousy for sleep Pressure Down here it's literal, but topside, it's just as heavy. It presses on your chest, on your thoughts until you're sure something's going to crack. This reef is dying.

Rising heat bleaches the coral, algae smothers it And the fish that fed the village are leaving Darkness Down here it swallows everything Sight, time, even your own voice Spend long enough in it and it starts to echo back at you.

Darkness down here, the road just eats headlights. People think they know where the lane is. And then it disappears on them Shine Everywhere you look, the city bounces itself back at you Sun, headlights, billboards. Doesn't matter. It's all glare.

Tickets come back soaked or bent from the dashboards The reader hates them, has to be coaxed everytime These barcodes peel up after a few years edges catch on other books, dust sticks and the scanner won’t read them
That back wheel on the cart Squeals like a mouse in a coffee can Spiders set up shop in these pits.

Rain keeps them happy and the glass gets fogged. You can't see the numbers unless you clear it. And I don't fancy putting my face too close Too much stillness These turbines are giants. But if the wind naps, the grid goes hungry.
Quiet air costs towns clean power I keep wanting the wind to behave Wind Up here it wipes footprints Words. Whole nights like they were never here.

Some days it feels like I'm the only thing it leaves behind. -What's your problem out here? Fresh snow stacks up on these slopes like glass plates A single vibration and the whole face can give way onto the highway or the village below
This shelf is fracturing. Warm water eats it from below. Cracks race inland, and when a slab the size of a city falls, it can throw a tsunami at the villages down coast
-What is the problem? We are losing centuries of climate memory Fragility
Down here, a whole universe of organisms survives by a thread One warm winter, one careless boot print and a lineage 3 million years old disappears Blocks of city concreter just sit here empty

old tunnels, sealed basements, miles of dead air meanwhile, we import food that travels farther than most people ever do Not enough room Everything is pressed in, people, smoke, horns, bills. You breathe, and somebody else is already using the air
The city doesn't stop pushing Too much room Out here, it’s valleys after valleys Sky stacked on sky Quite, big enough to get lost in you You drop a word and it doesn't land anywhere
Everything up here is pressed in wires, panels... People shouting from the street, ads shouting from the screens There's noise stacked on noise. Honestly,
the silence out here, it swallows everything When the engines off and the birds settle. It's just wind and my own heartbeat The noise
It's everywhere. Amps, generators... ummm The crowd The ringing in my ears when the night’s done Silence These guys are brilliant at following code,

but they don't laugh at my bad jokes or tell me when I look tired 12 hours in here in. The loudest thing is the air filter. Too much universe Every night this dish pulls in more data than I can catalog before the sun comes up.
